From: Elena Park <elena@brightline.com>

Subject: Edge connection flap causing surge in 5xx/429 errors

Rafael —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses this morning across our EU traffic (primarily eu-west-3). Peak error rate reached ~18% for tokenization endpoints and the dashboard shows repeated 502/503 bursts correlated with short connection flaps at the edge. The errors started around 07:50 UTC and have been intermittent since.

Attached: brightline_error_sample.log and ingress-trace-20270615.png show the spike and a sample trace where the client retried multiple times within a few seconds.

Impact: checkout flows degrade (timeouts) and some customers are reporting failed payments. This is high severity for us. Can your team triage immediately and confirm whether this is on Redwood’s ingress side or a downstream dependency? We also need a temporary mitigation while you investigate.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Ops — Brightline Payments

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Edge connection flap causing surge in 5xx/429 errors

Team — initial triage below (copying Elena’s original samples).

What I’m seeing:
- Short-lived TCP connection resets at our EU edge (03:50–03:58 local) that coincide with 502/503 returns from some upstream proxies.
- High request fanout from a subset of Brightline IPs with aggressive client retries (retry-after header missing / retry semantics are client-side). That pattern triggered our rate limiter and produced 429 responses which in turn caused more client retries — classic amplification.
- Not a downstream model container OOM — containers healthy and KV cache hit-rate stable.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:10 UTC):
1) Applied temporary circuit breaker on the most affected route to cap concurrent handoffs (reduced fanout).
2) Increased edge-worker capacity in eu-west-3 by +20% for the next 2 hours (manual scale).
3) Enabled a conservative retry-suppression header we support: X-Redwood-Max-Retry: 1 for that route via edge config.
4) Pushed a quick config change to prefer persistent connections to healthy upstreams (reduces transient handshakes).

Early results: error rate dropped from ~18% to ~6% within 15 minutes; 429s fell most dramatically. Some residual 502s remain in a few POPs where we saw repeated flaps.

Next steps I recommend now:
- Run an ingress-level packet capture on the two affected POPs (I’ll attach traces).
- Work with Brightline to reduce client retry aggressiveness (suggest exponential backoff and jitter).
- Postmortem and longer-term: add route-level backoff, improve health-check hysteresis on the edge load-balancer, and surface a per-customer retry policy in the Console.

I’ll continue to monitor. If error rate creeps up again we should fail-over traffic to an adjacent region while we stabilize the POPs.

— Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Thanks, Jonas — we applied the suggested client-side backoff change a few minutes ago and the volume of retries has dropped. We also ran a sanity check on our side (no recent deploys). We can confirm:
- Errors are reduced significantly (current visible error rate ~4%).
- A handful of customers still saw failed checkouts between 08:00–10:30 UTC.

Customer ask: Brightline is requesting a formal post-incident summary and a credit for partial downtime. They flagged this to their finance and account teams.

Please confirm ETA for a consolidated postmortem and whether Redwood will accept a joint incident review with Brightline. Also advise on next steps for credits/SLAs — I’ve copied Adam from CloudPath (procurement) who will coordinate contract-related items.

— Elena

Subject: Executive summary and next steps — Brightline edge incident (eu-west-3)

Folks — quick executive summary for leadership and the account team: 

What happened:
- Between ~07:50–10:15 UTC Brightline traffic to eu-west-3 experienced a burst of 502/503 errors and elevated 429s driven by short-lived connection flaps at two POPs combined with aggressive client retries. The retry amplification amplified load at the edge and tripped rate limits.

Impact:
- Peak error rate ~18% (reduced to ~4% after mitigations).
- Customer-facing: failed checkouts reported by a small subset of Brightline customers; Brightline has opened an internal finance/procurement request for credits.

Actions taken:
- Temporary circuit breaker and edge-worker scale (+20%) applied by SRE (Jonas).
- X-Redwood-Max-Retry header enforced for affected route; instructed Brightline to deploy client retry backoff (completed).
- Runbook steps executed; traces captured for postmortem.

Open items / asks for leadership:
- Approve a joint postmortem with Brightline (I recommend we proceed). I estimate a consolidated postmortem for them by EOD tomorrow (2027-06-16).
- Approve a goodwill credit range (I suggest 5–10% of June consumption for impacted windows) — we should discuss with Sales Ops and Finance.
- Review long-term mitigations: route-level backoff policies, improved LB health-check hysteresis, and per-customer retry policy in Console.

If approved I’ll schedule a joint incident review with Brightline and prepare the postmortem draft.

— Rafael Mendes
